title: Local negative-Ext vanishing and descent of morphisms between global derived objects
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal C$ be a set of open subsets covering $X$, and suppose $U\cap V=\bigcup_{W\in\mathcal C,\,W\subset U\cap V}W$ for all $U,V\in\mathcal C$. Let $M,N\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category] satisfy $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_U)}(M|_U,N|_U[i])=0$ for every $U\in\mathcal C$ and every integer $i<0$. For every open $O\subset X$ which is a union of members of $\mathcal C$, one has $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_O)}(M|_O,N|_O[i])=0$ for $i<0$. Moreover restriction is a bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_O)}(M|_O,N|_O)$ to the families $(a_U)_{U\in\mathcal C,\,U\subset O}$ with $a_U:M|_U\to N|_U$ and $a_U|_V=a_V$ whenever $V\subset U$ are in this indexing family. These assertions include $O=\varnothing$ and the empty covering family when $X=\varnothing$.

proof.text: Apply the quotient-map construction for the intersection-refining cover $\mathcal C$ to obtain a continuous map $f:X\to Y$ with $f^{-1}(f(U))=U$ and with the opens $f(U)$ forming a basis of $Y$. If $O$ is a union of members of $\mathcal C$, then $f(O)=\bigcup_{U\subset O}f(U)$ is open and $f^{-1}(f(O))=O$.

Set $\mathcal O_Y(V)=\mathcal O_X(f^{-1}V)$, with the inherited ring operations and restriction maps. A covering of $V$ pulls back to a covering of $f^{-1}V$, and inverse images preserve intersections; thus the sheaf equalizer axiom for $\mathcal O_X$ is the sheaf equalizer axiom for $\mathcal O_Y$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. The identity map $\mathcal O_Y\to f_*\mathcal O_X$ makes $f$ a morphism of ringed spaces [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. No locally ringed or scheme property is required of $Y$.

source.place: Tag 0D68 (cohomology-lemma-uniqueness), setting the auxiliary structure sheaf to the direct image

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-derived-basis-local-ext-sheaf] to the ringed-space morphism $f$ and the objects $M,N$. Its hypotheses hold on each basis open $f(U)$ because $f^{-1}(f(U))=U$ and the assumed local vanishing is exactly the required vanishing on $M|_U,N|_U$. Hence negative Hom vanishes on every open of $Y$, and $V\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(M|_{f^{-1}(V)},N|_{f^{-1}(V)})$ is a sheaf.

Write $F(V)=\operatorname{Hom}(M|_{f^{-1}V},N|_{f^{-1}V})$ for the sheaf just obtained, and $\mathcal C_O=\{U\in\mathcal C:U\subset O\}$. Step 1 gives a cover $f(O)=\bigcup_{U\in\mathcal C_O}f(U)$. For $U,V\in\mathcal C_O$ one has $f(U)\cap f(V)=f(U\cap V)$: if $y=f(x)\in f(U)\cap f(V)$, the equalities $f^{-1}f(U)=U$ and $f^{-1}f(V)=V$ put $x$ in both $U$ and $V$. The assumed refinement therefore covers this intersection by the $f(W)$ for $W\in\mathcal C$ with $W\subset U\cap V$. An inclusion-compatible family $a_U\in F(f(U))$ restricts from both $U$ and $V$ to $a_W$ on every such $f(W)$. The uniqueness clause of the sheaf axiom [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] makes the restrictions equal on $f(U)\cap f(V)$. Its existence clause glues them to a unique section of $F(f(O))$. Since $f^{-1}f(O)=O$, this is precisely the required map on $O$. Conversely restrictions of a global map satisfy the inclusion equations by composition of restriction; uniqueness of gluing makes the two operations inverse.

Apply the all-open vanishing conclusion of [lem-trf-derived-basis-local-ext-sheaf] to $f(O)$, using $f^{-1}f(O)=O$, to obtain the asserted negative-degree vanishing. The sheaf axiom for the empty cover says $F(\varnothing)$ is a singleton, so Step 4 also applies when $O=\varnothing$ and its indexing family is empty. If that family contains the empty open, its only map is again the unique section of $F(\varnothing)$. If $X=\varnothing$ and $\mathcal C$ is empty, the topological basis in Step 1 is empty and covers $Y$, so $Y=\varnothing$; the same argument applies without any nonemptiness assumption.
